questions.question: In which city was Thomas Edison born?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Edison was born in Milan, Ohio.
Incorrect. The article says he grew up in Port Huron, Michigan, but was born in Milan, Ohio.
Incorrect. Newark, New Jersey is where he owned a telegraph recorder factory, not where he was born.
Incorrect. New York City is where he moved at age 22 to focus on engineering, not his birthplace.

questions.question: How many patents did Edison register in the United States?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Edison registered 1,093 patents in the United States.
Incorrect. The article does not mention 100 patents; it states 1,093.
Incorrect. The article does not mention 10,000 patents; it states 1,093.
Incorrect. The article does not mention 500 patents; it states 1,093.

questions.question: What nickname was Edison known by at Menlo Park?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article refers to Edison as 'The Wizard of Menlo Park'.
Incorrect. 'The Wizard of Oz' is not mentioned in the article.
Incorrect. The article does not call him 'The Inventor of Newark'.
Incorrect. The article does not call him 'The Genius of New York'; it says he grew to resent titles representing him as a genius.

questions.question: Which company was formed by the merger of Edison General Electric Company and Thomson-Houston Electric Company?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states the merger resulted in the formation of General Electric.
Incorrect. Westinghouse Electric was a competitor, not the result of the merger.
Incorrect. Western Union is mentioned as an employer, not as the result of the merger.
Incorrect. Bell Telephone is not mentioned as being formed by this merger.

questions.question: At what age did Edison develop hearing problems?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Edison developed hearing problems at the age of 12.
Incorrect. The article does not say he developed hearing problems at age 5.
Incorrect. Age 22 is when he moved to New York City, not when he developed hearing problems.
Incorrect. Age 29 is when he owned a telegraph recorder factory, not when he developed hearing problems.

questions.question: What was Edison's first patent for?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states his first patent was for the electric vote recorder.
Incorrect. The phonograph was invented later, not his first patent.
Incorrect. The incandescent light bulb was not his first patent.
Incorrect. The carbon microphone was developed later, not his first patent.

questions.question: In what year did Edison demonstrate the phonograph before the National Academy of Sciences?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Edison demonstrated the phonograph before the National Academy of Sciences in April 1878.
Incorrect. 1877 is when he first gained wider notice for the phonograph, not the demonstration year.
Incorrect. 1876 is when he set out to improve telephones, not the phonograph demonstration year.
Incorrect. 1880 is not mentioned as the year of the demonstration.

questions.question: What did Edison's first phonograph record on?
options: tinfoil wrapped around a grooved cylinder
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states his first phonograph recorded on tinfoil wrapped around a grooved cylinder.
Incorrect. Wax-coated cardboard cylinders were used by Bell and others in the 1880s, not Edison's first phonograph.
Incorrect. Magnetic tape is not mentioned in the article.
Incorrect. Vinyl records are not mentioned in the article.

questions.question: Which company did Edison establish that was never profitable?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Edison simultaneously created a mining company, which was never profitable.
Incorrect. General Electric was formed by a merger and was not described as never profitable.
Incorrect. Western Union was an employer and financier, not Edison's unprofitable company.
Incorrect. The Edison Phonograph Company was founded later and is not described as never profitable in the same way.

questions.question: What was Edison's last obsession?
options: the search for domestic rubber production
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states his last obsession was the search for domestic rubber production.
Incorrect. Motion pictures were an earlier area of work, not his last obsession.
Incorrect. Electric power distribution was an earlier area of work, not his last obsession.
Incorrect. The phonograph was an earlier invention, not his last obsession.
